title: Calls, texts & voice notes
goal: Answer and end calls naturally, cope with a bad line, say you'll call back, text and send voice notes, and say what you've already done, are still doing or haven't done yet.
intro:
In India the phone rings more than it buzzes: people call for everything, and when they don't call they send a WhatsApp voice note. This unit gives you the phone Hindi you'll use every day: **हाँ, बोलो** 'yes, go ahead', **आवाज़ नहीं आ रही** 'I can't hear you', **कॉल कट गया** 'the call dropped', **चलो, रखता हूँ** 'OK, bye'.

Two pieces of grammar make your sentences flow: the **-कर** form for 'do X and then Y' (**पहुँचकर मैसेज करना** 'text when you get there'), and the words for **just, already, still** and **not yet** (**मैं कॉल कर चुका हूँ**, **उसने अभी तक रिप्लाई नहीं किया**).

grammar.title: Do X and then Y: the -कर form
grammar.body:
English links actions with 'and (then)': *I'll eat and call you*. Hindi puts the first verb in the **conjunctive participle**: verb stem + **कर**, and only the last verb carries the tense:

खाना **खाकर** कॉल करूँगा 'I'll call after eating' (lit. 'having eaten, I'll call').

**Forms**: पहुँचना → **पहुँचकर**, लेना → **लेकर**, बैठना → **बैठकर**. In everyday speech **-के** is just as common: **खाके**, **पहुँचके**. One exception: करना → **करके** (never करकर).

**Uses**:
**Sequence** — घर **पहुँचकर** फ़ोन करना 'call when you get home'.
**Manner / how** — **बैठकर** बात करो 'sit down and talk'; **लेकर आना** 'to bring' (lit. come having taken).
**By doing** — मैसेज **करके** बता दो 'let them know by text'.

Both actions have the **same subject**, and whether you need ने depends only on the **last** verb: **मैं** खाना खाकर **सो गया** (no ने: सोना), but **मैंने** खाना खाकर **फ़ोन किया** (ने: करना).

The trap: don't add और between them — खाकर और कॉल करूँगा is wrong. And remember **करके**.

examples.en: I'll call when I get home.

examples.en: Try a video call, it might get through.

grammar.title: Just, already, still, not yet
grammar.body:
**Just (now)**: **अभी-अभी** + past: उसका मैसेज **अभी-अभी** आया 'his message just came'.

**Already** — two ways:
(1) verb stem + **चुका / चुकी / चुके** + हूँ / है / था: मैं खा **चुका** हूँ 'I've already eaten'. चुकना never stands alone, and it takes **no ने** even with transitive verbs: **मैं** बता चुकी हूँ (not मैंने).
(2) **पहले ही** + an ordinary past: मैंने **पहले ही** बता दिया था 'I had already told them'.

**Still**: **अब भी / अभी भी** + present or continuous: वो **अब भी** सो रहा है 'he's still asleep'. **अभी तक** also means 'still' in positive sentences: तुम अभी तक वहीं हो? 'you're still there?'

**Not yet**: **अभी तक … नहीं** + past: उसने **अभी तक** रिप्लाई **नहीं** किया 'he hasn't replied yet'. The short answer is **अभी नहीं** 'not yet'.

**Yet?** in a question usually needs no word at all — the compound verb does the job: पहुँच **गए**? 'are you there (yet)?', खाना खा **लिया**? 'have you eaten (yet)?'

The trap: अब भी / अभी तक, not just अभी — **अभी** alone means 'now'.

dialogue.title: Lost on the way to a party
dialogue.setting: Lucknow. Nikhil is on his way to Ayesha's birthday dinner and can't find her house. The line is bad.

lines.roman: bahut dhīre. zarā zor se bolo!

lines.roman: achchhā, vahāṃ koī dukān dikh rahī hai?

lines.speaker: Ayesha
lines.native: कॉल कट गया। वॉइस नोट भेज रही हूँ: मिठाई की दुकान से बाएँ मुड़कर तीसरा घर।

lines.en: (voice note) The call dropped. I'm sending a voice note: turn left at the sweet shop, it's the third house.

lines.native: मिल गया! वैसे, मिठाई लेकर आऊँ?
lines.roman: mil gayā! vaise, miṭhāī lekar āūṃ?
lines.en: (voice note) Found it! By the way, shall I bring some sweets?

lines.en: OK, but don't call again, just ring the bell!

culture: Indians phone a lot more than they text, and a call usually starts without small talk: **हाँ, बोलो** 'yes, tell me' is a perfectly friendly way to answer. With elders and strangers answer **जी, बोलिए** or **हेलो जी**. Calls end with a little ritual: **चलो, रखता हूँ** / **रखती हूँ** 'OK, I'll put it down', **और कुछ?** 'anything else?', **बाय**. The **missed call** is a language of its own: ringing once on purpose means 'I've arrived', 'come down' or 'call me back, I'm out of credit'. In messages, most people write Hindi in **Roman letters** ('kya kar rahe ho?', 'ok, aata hoon') rather than Devanagari, and **voice notes** are hugely popular because they're faster than typing. Family WhatsApp groups are famous for good-morning images and forwarded messages from parents and uncles, and leaving a message on 'seen' without replying can cause real offence.

tip.title: Phone manners
tip.body:
- Answer a friend with **हाँ, बोलो** 'yes, go ahead'; an elder or stranger with **जी, बोलिए**.
- Unknown caller: **हेलो, कौन बोल रहा है?** (polite: **कौन बोल रहे हैं?**).
- **फ़ोन उठाना** = to answer, **फ़ोन काटना** = to cut someone off.
- Wind up with **चलो, रखता हूँ** (woman: **रखती हूँ**).

lessons.title: Can you hear me?

tip.title: Hearing on the phone
tip.body:
- Hindi talks about the **sound**: (मेरी) आवाज़ **आ रही है**? 'can you hear me?' (lit. is my voice coming?). आवाज़ is feminine: आ **रही** है.
- Or **मुझे … सुनाई देना**: मुझे सुनाई नहीं दे रहा 'I can't hear'.
- A call 'connects' with **लगना**: फ़ोन नहीं लग रहा 'can't get through'.
- It drops with **कटना**: कॉल **कट** गया.

lessons.title: I'll call you when…

tip.title: Do X and then Y: -कर
tip.body:
- Stem + **कर** = 'having done': **खाकर** 'after eating', **पहुँचकर** 'once you get there'. In speech also **-के**: खाके.
- Only the last verb has a tense: घर पहुँचकर फ़ोन **करूँगा**.
- करना → **करके**, never करकर.
- No और in between, and both verbs share one subject.

tip.title: English word + करना
tip.body:
- Most messaging words are English nouns + **करना**: मैसेज करना, रिप्लाई करना, टाइप करना, फ़ॉरवर्ड करना, सेव करना, व्हाट्सऐप करना.
- The English word never changes; करना does the grammar: रिप्लाई **किया**, फ़ॉरवर्ड **कर दो**.
- Reply **to** something: X **का** रिप्लाई करना. On WhatsApp: व्हाट्सऐप **पर**.

sentences.en: No time to type, I'm sending a voice note. (woman speaking)

sentences.roman: merā nambar sev kar lo, maiṃ Ravi hūṃ.
sentences.en: Save my number, it's Ravi.

sentences.native: मम्मी हर सुबह ग्रुप में मैसेज फ़ॉरवर्ड करती हैं।
sentences.roman: mammī har subah grup meṃ maisej forvarḍ kartī haiṃ.
sentences.en: Mum forwards messages to the group every morning.

sentences.native: इतना लंबा वॉइस नोट? मैं बाद में सुनूँगा।
sentences.roman: itnā lambā vois noṭ? maiṃ bād meṃ sunūṃgā.
sentences.en: Such a long voice note? I'll listen later.

sentences.native: ठीक है, घर पहुँचकर व्हाट्सऐप कर देना।
sentences.roman: ṭhīk hai, ghar pahuṃchkar Vhāṭsaip kar denā.
sentences.en: OK, just WhatsApp me when you get home.

sentences.native: मैसेज देखा, लेकिन रिप्लाई करना भूल गया।
sentences.roman: maisej dekhā, lekin riplāī karnā bhūl gayā.
sentences.en: I saw the message but forgot to reply.

tip.title: चुका, अब भी, अभी तक नहीं
tip.body:
- **Already**: stem + **चुका / चुकी / चुके**: मैं कॉल कर **चुका** हूँ. No ने with चुका! Or **पहले ही** + past.
- **Just**: **अभी-अभी** + past.
- **Still**: **अब भी** (or अभी भी): वो **अब भी** सो रहा है.
- **Not yet**: **अभी तक … नहीं**: उसने **अभी तक** नहीं देखा. Short answer: **अभी नहीं**.
tip.pattern: stem + चुका हूँ  ·  अभी तक … नहीं

sentences.native: मैं उसे पाँच बार कॉल कर चुका हूँ।
sentences.roman: maiṃ use pāṃch bār kol kar chukā hūṃ.
sentences.en: I've already called him five times. (man speaking)

sentences.native: मैं पहले ही बता चुकी हूँ कि मैं नहीं आऊँगी।
sentences.roman: maiṃ pahle hī batā chukī hūṃ ki maiṃ nahīṃ āūṃgī.
sentences.en: I've already said I won't come. (woman speaking)

sentences.native: तुम्हारे पाँच मिस्ड कॉल थे, क्या हुआ?
sentences.roman: tumhāre pāṃch misḍ kol the, kyā huā?
sentences.en: I had five missed calls from you, what happened?

sentences.native: वो अब भी सो रहा है, फ़ोन नहीं उठा रहा।
sentences.roman: vo ab bhī so rahā hai, fon nahīṃ uṭhā rahā.
sentences.en: He's still asleep, he isn't picking up.

sentences.native: उसने अभी तक मेरा मैसेज नहीं देखा।
sentences.roman: usne abhī tak merā maisej nahīṃ dekhā.
sentences.en: She hasn't seen my message yet.

sentences.native: लोकेशन भेज दो, मैं रास्ते में हूँ।
sentences.roman: lokeshan bhej do, maiṃ rāste meṃ hūṃ.
sentences.en: Send me the location, I'm on my way.

sentences.native: तुम अभी तक घर नहीं पहुँचे?
sentences.roman: tum abhī tak ghar nahīṃ pahuṃche?
sentences.en: You haven't got home yet?

sentences.native: मैंने पहले ही टिकट ले लिए हैं।
sentences.roman: maiṃne pahle hī ṭikaṭ le liye haiṃ.
sentences.en: I've already got the tickets.

sentences.native: मैंने उसे अभी-अभी लोकेशन भेजी है।
sentences.roman: maiṃne use abhī-abhī lokeshan bhejī hai.
sentences.en: I've just sent her the location.

sentences.native: अभी नहीं, बस पहुँचने वाला हूँ।
sentences.roman: abhī nahīṃ, bas pahuṃchne vālā hūṃ.
sentences.en: Not yet, I'm almost there.
